what_was_mock_or_missing_before: the library shipped four SGS closures with no comparative case at all; the only LES benchmark (benchmarks/cbc_dit_les) exercises Smagorinsky alone and there was no degeneracy/negative control

laminar_degeneracy.criterion: WALE modelled stress in laminar flow (uniform / linear shear / Poiseuille)
laminar_degeneracy.note: WALE is built from grad(u)^2, so for any unidirectional shear the traceless symmetric part vanishes identically (S^d = 0); the frozen analytic profiles are the probes and the LBM Stokes wave is the dynamic control (nu_eff/nu=1.005919)

a_spectrum_slope.criterion: spectral slope at station 98 vs the CBC 1971 measurement fitted over the same resolved k-window
a_spectrum_slope.note: max |slope_LBM - slope_CBC| over 1 cases; the textbook inertial-range window k*eta in [0.1, 1] is NOT reachable on these grids (largest resolved k*eta = 0.206, since eta = 2.60e-04 m against a 0.508 m box), so the anchor is the measurement itself; finest completed grids evaluated: {'smagorinsky': 128}; runs excluded as diverged: ['dynamic_smagorinsky:n32(0.49)', 'dynamic_smagorinsky:n64(0.25)', 'dynamic_smagorinsky:n128(0.14)', 'wale:n64(0.35)', 'wale:n128(0.27)', 'vreman:n64(0.34)', 'vreman:n128(0.22)']; literal-window fits: {'smagorinsky': nan}

b_decay_exponent.criterion: TKE decay exponent n (k ~ t^-n) vs the CBC 1971 measured exponent
b_decay_exponent.note: relative error in percent, worst of the four closures; the CBC exponent is fitted from the three tabulated measured spectra

c_tgv_dissipation_peak.criterion: Taylor-Green eps(t) peak vs the spectral DNS at the same Re
c_tgv_dissipation_peak.note: DNS eps_max=0.01279 at t*=6.00 (n=64, grid-converged to 0.005829016); per-model errors %: {('smagorinsky', 64): 11.65, ('dynamic_smagorinsky', 64): 13.42, ('wale', 64): 12.43, ('vreman', 64): 12.6}

d_dynamic_cs.criterion: dynamic Smagorinsky Cs^2 adapts: > 0 in turbulence, = 0 in laminar flow
d_dynamic_cs.reference: 0 < Cs^2 <= 0.1 in turbulence; Cs^2 == 0 in laminar
d_dynamic_cs.note: TGV n=64: max Cs^2=0 (Cs=0.000); laminar Poiseuille: Cs^2=3.311e-28

f_vreman_laminar_degeneracy.criterion: Vreman modelled stress in laminar flow (linear shear / Poiseuille)
f_vreman_laminar_degeneracy.note: Vreman's invariant B_beta vanishes for any two-dimensional (x-invariant) shear, so the closure is exactly zero there, including in the LBM Stokes wave (nu_eff/nu=1.005919)

g_negative_controls.criterion: SGS off -> plain BGK (DNS) and Delta -> 0 -> nu_t -> 0
g_negative_controls.note: C_s=0 / C_w=0 / C_v=0 trajectories are identical to the plain BGK run to 0.00e+00 (bit-level, same kernel); nu_t/nu at fixed physical flow falls as n^{-1.465107} over the grid levels that survive the run (Delta = dx -> 0); the O(Delta^2) law is 2, and only two levels are usable here because the non-static closures diverge in this configuration

h_grid_convergence.criterion: CBC spectra agree across the grid ladder (spectral integral error, large-scale window)
h_grid_convergence.note: per-pair errors {'32vs64': 0.3009287, '32vs128': 0.4413437, '64vs128': 0.2818696}; the 64 vs 128 pair (both resolving the same scales) is 0.2818696. Where 32^3 disagrees the note is the measured resolution: dx/eta = {32: 60.9589, 64: 30.47945, 128: 15.23972} per grid
